jamie: Customer (Acme) reports intermittent 401s when opening an SSE stream. Root request-id they provided: rq_0a1b2c3d. They say token TTL looks ok. Need minimal cURL repro + traces to escalate.

lucy: Ok — ask them for exact request-id(s) + UTC time window. Also confirm whether they're going through a corporate proxy or WAF. For streaming repro we typically need: --no-buffer, Accept: text/event-stream, and --trace-ascii.

jamie: Got more info from customer: request-ids = [rq_0a1b2c3d, rq_0f9e8d7c], window 2026-03-10T14:23:00Z -> 14:26:00Z. They are behind an enterprise proxy (Fiddler). They tried curl but only captured "connection closed".

raj: Sounds like proxy is dropping keepalives or mutating auth. Ask them to run this exact minimal repro and attach /tmp/curl.trace: 

```
curl --http2 --no-buffer \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN_REDACTED>" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: rq_0a1b2c3d" \
  "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/streams/chat?model=gpt-mini" \
  --trace-ascii /tmp/curl.trace \
  --include --silent
```

raj: In the trace we want the HTTP/2 frames and any RST_STREAM/GOAWAY. If possible also run tcpdump on client (capture port 443 for that time window).

kevin: Also try bypassing the proxy once (direct network) to see if issue disappears. If proxy is required, ask for proxy config (timeout, max-conns). Small tip: include --raw to see raw bytes when using curl: `--raw`.

jamie: Customer pasted a short excerpt from curl.trace: 

```
== Info: Connected to api.redwood-inference.com (10.0.0.5) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/streams/chat?model=gpt-mini HTTP/2
> accept: text/event-stream
> authorization: Bearer ***REDACTED***
> x-request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d
< HTTP/2 200 \'text/event-stream\'
< content-type: text/event-stream
< x-request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d
: event: message\n: data: {"chunk":"hello"}\n
# ~30s later
< HTTP/2 401
< content-type: application/json
< x-request-id: rq_0f9e8d7c
{"error":"unauthorized","code":"invalid_token"}
```

lucy: Good capture — we see a 200 then a later 401 with a different request-id. That matches a mid-stream token validation or proxy session swap. Ask for server logs for both request-ids and the auth service logs for the TTL during window.

raj: Checklist to request from customer (please DM a secure upload link):
- /tmp/curl.trace (from the exact command above)
- raw tcpdump (pcap) covering the window 2026-03-10T14:22:30Z -> 14:26:30Z
- proxy config and proxy logs around that time
- the exact curl command they ran (copy/paste) and the shell environment (curl version)
- any client-side reconnect logic or middleware that might re-send a new token mid-stream
- note of whether they use short-lived tokens + automatic refresh

ingest-bot: Please run `support:collect-debug-bundle --request-id=rq_0a1b2c3d,rq_0f9e8d7c --window=2026-03-10T14:22:00Z/2026-03-10T14:27:00Z` to gather server-side traces and auth checks.

kevin: If customer can't share pcap, at minimum get the curl.trace and proxy logs. Also ask them to add `-H "X-Client-Side-Timestamp: $(date --utc +%FT%TZ)"` so we can align events.

jamie: I'll send the checklist + minimal repro to the customer and request an upload link. Will DM ingest-bot when files are uploaded. Thanks — will update when I have the bundle. :thumbsup:

lucy: One more quick validation: ask them to re-run with a freshly minted token and include the token creation time. If the token is being refreshed client-side, a race could produce a late-change mid-connection.

jamie: noted, will include that step in the message.
